paraphrases: Apply one instruction to the supplied registers. Registers are integers modulo 97. swap exchanges {register} and {other} simultaneously. add adds {value} to {register}. mix adds (2 times {other} plus {value}) to {register}. conditional adds {value} if {other} is greater than {threshold}, otherwise subtracts {value}. Reduce updated numeric registers modulo 97; preserve other registers. Return only the complete resulting registers as a JSON object.

You are given registers holding integers modulo 97 and one instruction. swap: the registers named by {register} and {other} exchange values at the same time. add: the {register} register increases by {value}. mix: the {register} register increases by twice the {other} register plus {value}. conditional: if the {other} register is strictly greater than {threshold}, the {register} register increases by {value}; otherwise it decreases by {value}. Reduce every updated register modulo 97 and leave the rest unchanged. Output only the complete resulting registers as a JSON object.

Execute the single instruction on the registers (integers modulo 97). swap - exchange the {register} and {other} registers simultaneously; add - add {value} to the {register} register; mix - add 2 x the {other} register + {value} to the {register} register; conditional - when the {other} register is greater than {threshold}, add {value} to the {register} register, else subtract {value} from it. Each updated register is reduced modulo 97; untouched registers keep their values. Reply with only the complete resulting registers as a JSON object.

Registers are integers modulo 97. Carry out the one instruction given. For swap, the {register} and {other} registers trade values simultaneously. For add, {value} is added to the {register} register. For mix, the {register} register gains two times the {other} register plus {value}. For conditional, the {register} register gains {value} if the {other} register is greater than {threshold} and loses {value} otherwise. Take updated registers modulo 97 and keep the others as they are. Return just the complete resulting registers as a JSON object.

Update the registers by applying the single instruction below; every register holds an integer modulo 97. A swap instruction makes the {register} and {other} registers exchange their values at once. An add instruction increases the {register} register by {value}. A mix instruction increases the {register} register by {value} plus double the {other} register. A conditional instruction increases the {register} register by {value} when the {other} register exceeds {threshold}, and decreases it by {value} when it does not. Every changed register is reduced modulo 97, and every other register stays the same. Respond with nothing but the full set of resulting registers as one JSON object.

go_rule: PRE-STATED SCREEN GO RULE, REVISION 6 (T2b-register; supersedes revisions 1-5, stated before any output exists; seed by seed; point estimates on the fresh dev screen bank, decided EXACTLY on integer counts as rationals (no floating-point rounding: a difference or share equal to a bar meets a '>=' bar and does not meet a '<' bar); 95% cluster-bootstrap CIs reported, not gating; every condition component decided within one bootstrap SE of its bar is flagged in the report). TRAINING: the surface-diversity build 'sd' only (decision point 1 fired: PREREG-3 TRIGGER): the same 750 rows, each prompt rendered with a seeded rule-text paraphrase (0-3), field names (variants 0-3 per field) and JSON key orders drawn from a TRAIN subset of permutations per object type (top level, state, event); paraphrase 4, field-name variant 4 and the HELD-OUT key orders (per object type the fully reversed canonical order plus 2 fixed seeded permutations where they exist; the 2-key top level has only its reversed order, so it trains in the canonical order alone) never occur in training; targets keep the literal cmp -> calc -> after order. Outcome = exact 'after' state (the decision parser reads only 'after'; a malformed trace/filler answer is wrong). Two renderings of the same rows, paired by row: IN-SURFACE = Titan's verbatim one-step frame; HELD-OUT SURFACE (HS) = paraphrase 4 + field-name variant 4 + a held-out key order per object type, rotating over the held-out orders by row, on the primary strata and on the three identification strata. PRIMARY outcomes are out of range (joint amendment 5): 'conditional' = cond_oor_val + cond_oor_thr + cond_far pooled (branch-balanced pairs; cond_far = in-range values and thresholds with |other - threshold| 16..96, beyond every training row's 0..15); 'cond_oor_val' = the boundary pairs alone (other = threshold: ok false; other = threshold + 1: ok true); 'mix' = mix_oor. IDENTIFICATION strata (G1 only; none is pooled into 'conditional'): 'cond_sametens' = 50 branch-balanced minimal pairs with tens(other) == tens(threshold), so the branch is decided by the units digit, |other - threshold| in 2..9 (2..7 realized: both members of a pair lie in one decade), |value| 12..40 (out of range), in-range registers and thresholds, neither branch wraps; it separates the comparison from tens-digit shortcuts that are exact on every primary conditional row (e.g. 'add iff tens(other) > tens(threshold) or other == threshold + 1' scores 1/2 on it); 'cond_oor_edge' (revision 5) = 20 branch-balanced minimal quadruples at the boundary of the env's strict 'other > threshold': other - threshold = -1 and 0 (ok false) and +1 and +2 (ok true), |value| 12..40 (out of range), in-range registers and thresholds, neither branch wraps, 10 quadruples moving the threshold and 10 the other register; with cond_oor_val it gives G1 rows at other = threshold - 1, threshold and threshold + 1, so every off-by-one variant of the comparison (one that differs from it only at other = threshold - 1, threshold or threshold + 1, e.g. '>=', '> threshold + 1', '>= threshold - 1', 'or other == threshold - 1') is contradicted on at least 1/4 of its rows; 'cond_adv' (revision 6) = 100 rows, 50 ok true and 50 ok false, drawn by seeded rejection sampling over valid conditional rows (other 0..96, threshold -40..136, |value| 12..40, neither branch wraps) to fixed quotas of 15 design types: 13 signature classes of the extended shortcut family H (sets of (other, threshold) cells on which exactly the same members of H are wrong), one of them split by digit lengths, covering sign-crossing cells, cross-length cells (1 vs 2, 2 vs 1, 1 vs 3 and 2 vs 3 digits), cross-decade cells whose units comparison disagrees with the tens comparison and cells at other - threshold = -3, -2, +3, +4; H (scripts/t2br_shortcuts.py, DESIGN.md section 15; 3,519 predicates) = the enumerated digit and off-by-one family with its modifiers at other = threshold - 1, threshold and threshold + 1 (3,483 predicates, the branch-blind constants included) + lexicographic string comparison with and without sign handling, digit-sum, units-only and tens-only comparisons with sign- and length-aware variants, magnitude-only |other| > |threshold| and the isolated single-distance exceptions at |other - threshold| = 2..4; on cond_adv every member of H that differs from the comparison somewhere on that domain and passes revision 5's G1 against a plain arm at 0 is wrong on at least 33 rows, except the isolated distance exceptions, of which those at other - threshold = -3, -2, +3 and +4 are wrong on exactly 21 (the operator's target, every member of H wrong on at least 40 rows, is infeasible on any 100-row branch-balanced stratum: five members of H have pairwise-disjoint error sets). PREDICATE ACCURACY (trace side; arithmetic-independent): the share of a stratum's rows whose trace answer the strict joint parser accepts, whose cmp is an object with exactly the keys x, thr, ok in that literal order, and whose ok is a JSON boolean equal to the env's predicate (other > threshold) for that row; x and thr are not scored; a malformed trace or a wrong key order counts as wrong. FILLER (amendment 4b): the fill length is a per-kind constant: the smallest run of ' .' units such that the filler target is at least as long (Titan tokens) as the LONGEST trace target of that kind over train + dev (one-step rows and the chains' gold steps), whatever its 'after' (swap 7, add 17, mix 17, conditional 29 units); every filler target of a kind is identical up to 'after', so its length carries no information about the answer. VALIDITY: format_ok = the strict joint parser accepts the answer; the trace (filler) side is valid iff its in-surface format_ok >= 0.95 on each primary. DECISION POINT 3 (checked first): if trace - filler < 0.10 on BOTH in-surface primaries, STOP: 'trace ~ filler, not supervision of the intermediates (an answer-free filler of constant length per action kind, amendment 4b, does as well: the gain is attributable to extra decode positions or the answer format)', with the sub-label 'trace format failed' if the trace side is not valid, else 'filler control invalid' if the filler side is not valid, else 'neither format helped' if filler - plain < 0.10 on both in-surface primaries. Otherwise GO iff ALL of: (G1) trace - plain >= +0.25 on conditional, on cond_oor_val alone, on cond_oor_edge alone AND on cond_sametens alone, AND the trace side's predicate accuracy >= 0.80 on cond_oor_edge alone, on cond_sametens alone AND on cond_adv alone (cond_adv has no trace - plain clause), each both in-surface and on the held-out surface (the predicate clauses have no plain-arm term, so a plain arm that is weak on the out-of-range arithmetic cannot let through a member of H that they catch; G1 excludes the members of H, documented by the enumeration over H against three plain baselines (DRYRUN.json shortcut_enumeration: every member of H that differs from the comparison, except the isolated exception 'other > threshold or other == threshold - 4', which passes every G1 part); it cannot exclude every conceivable heuristic); (G2) trace - plain >= +0.30 on mix, both in-surface and on the held-out surface; (G3) filler below trace: trace - filler >= +0.10 on EACH in-surface primary; (G4) controls: trace ON - OFF >= -0.05 on swap and on add_nowrap (untouched skills; in-surface); (G5) in-distribution non-inferiority: trace - plain >= -0.05 on conditional_in (branch-balanced mean over cond_xm1, cond_x0, cond_xp1, cond_mid) and on mix_in (in-surface); and the filler side is valid. If G1-G5 all hold but the filler side is not valid: INCONCLUSIVE: filler control invalid. Otherwise NO-GO, naming every failed condition and its failed parts. Reported, not gating: the held-out-surface results of the OFF and filler sides; the surface audit (held-out minus in-surface, paired by row, every side and held-out-surface stratum); the filler residual covariate (constant filler tokens minus that row's trace tokens) with the filler side's accuracy split at its median; the shortcut-agreement analysis (the trace side's cmp.ok against the env's predicate and against every member of H over all conditional rows of the dev bank, in each rendering: 'SHORTCUT_CONSISTENT' if a member of H that differs from the predicate on those rows agrees with the trace's cmp.ok at least as well as the predicate does; it never changes the verdict and is quoted with any GO); per-factor held-out renderings (paraphrase only, names only, key order only) are omitted by choice (a GPU-budget choice, not a capacity limit). LIMITS, quoted with every statement of the verdict: G1 identifies the comparison only against H (it excludes the members of H that the enumeration shows failing it, not every conceivable heuristic); the isolated exception 'other > threshold or other == threshold - 4' passes G1 (on any 100-row branch-balanced stratum one of the exceptions at -4, -3, -2 passes the 0.80 bar); per-factor held-out renderings are omitted; a GO is a seed-0 screen result. The screen is seed 0; the roadmap's confirmation requires the same rule in all 3 seeds before a sealed R bank is built.
